question.text: Geopolitical risk differs from country risk primarily because:

answer.text: Geopolitical risk focuses on international relations/conflicts; country risk focuses on domestic economic/political stability
Country risk applies only to frontier markets

explanation.text: The Logic: Country risk arises from a country's political and economic environment, while geopolitical risk arises from relationships with neighbouring or other countries and regional groupings; such geopolitical risks can be long-term and are often already priced in. The Trap: Both risks can coexist for the same country and are not interchangeable. Note: Source: NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook, p.22, p.285.
